summary: The article presents the Paradigm framework at the University of Illinois, which combines automatic data partitioning, communication optimization, irregular-computation runtime support, functional parallelism and multithreading for distributed-memory multicomputers. It illustrates each component with kernels and reports measured busy and overhead times and speedups on the CM-5, Paragon and IBM SP-1.
why_read: It is a short 1995 overview of one research compiler that brings together most of the regular, irregular and task-parallel techniques of the period in a single framework.
main_contribution: An integrated description of the Paradigm framework's partitioning, communication optimization, irregular runtime and multithreading components.
main_limitation: The authors state that integrating all capabilities into the framework is still in progress, and results are shown only for kernels and selected applications.
evaluation_method: Measured busy and overhead time breakdowns and speedups on 32- and 64-processor machines, compared against serial and SPMD baselines

evidence.section: Irregular computations; Functional and data parallelism; Multithreading
